thesis: Status-quo anchor on the Silver Bulletin net approval of -22.3 (16 Oct 2026), near a record low, with a ~4-point SD over 75 days for midterm and other shocks.

Midterm penalty for the president's party, a 5-11 point Democratic generic-ballot lead and a razor-thin starting majority put Democratic control near 90%, matching Kalshi and Polymarket at 90-92%. Most sensitive to a late generic-ballot reversal; Other (a tie) is negligible.

No founding member has ever triggered Article 50, no process is pending, and the window is about 10 weeks. Markets for any EU member leaving price a few percent. The forecast is most sensitive to a government announcing a binding exit vote or a formal notice, and none is visible.

Noem, Bondi and Gabbard have already left (3 certain on a literal reading), and markets imply about 1.6 more exits among the remaining 12 before 2027, with a right tail from a possible post-midterm shakeup.

58% of best-of-seven World Series since 1905 reached a Game 6 (68/117, Baseball-Reference), and 54% did from 2000 to 2025. A game-by-game model using the Brewers' ~61% title odds after removing the bookmaker margin (DraftKings -170) gives ~60%. The forecast is most sensitive to how big Milwaukee's per-game edge over the AL champion really is: a bigger edge makes a sweep or a 4-1 result more likely.

GDPNow sits at 3.6% (Oct 15), and Polymarket and Kalshi put about 65-70% on a print of 3.0% or more, which centres the advance estimate near 3.3% once GDPNow's usual overshoot is allowed for. The tails are wide because the nowcast rests on a large inventory build (+1.9pp) offset by a large net-export drag (-2.7pp), and the Q2 advance print missed its nowcasts by more than 1pp.

Advisory committees side with sponsors about 60% of the time, but less often after an FDA rejection. Here the rejection is efficacy-only, the trial met its primary endpoint with a clean safety profile, clinical consensus is pro-atropine, and the panel was convened through the sponsor's formal dispute, which tilts a benefit-risk vote toward YES. The forecast is most sensitive to how harshly the FDA briefing frames the modest 0.01% effect and the missing axial-length data.

I treat the index as a random walk from the live level of about 5,607 on Oct 19 (Yahoo Finance) over about 8.5 sessions. The spread comes from 2026's extreme volatility, roughly 3.2% a day after the chip sell-off and circuit breaker on Oct 15. The forecast is most sensitive to whether that volatility persists or fades.

A random walk from the ~$61 October 16 close (Yahoo Finance), 9 sessions out, with about 120% annualised volatility and fat tails, because the stock is in a credit-stress episode (2032 bonds near a 15% yield, record CDS). Short-covering and 'overblown' calls roughly offset financing and contagion risk, so the median is not tilted. The forecast is most sensitive to any new financing or distress news before October 29.

Northeast Pacific ACE is 343.1 (Climatlas, Oct 19), and the dying Hurricane Trudy should add only ~3 more units (NHC). That leaves the total near 346, so YES most likely needs the low south of Guatemala (NHC: 90% 7-day formation chance) to become a tropical storm or hurricane worth ~4+ ACE before Oct 29. The forecast is most sensitive to whether 343.1 already includes Trudy's Oct 18 fixes.

Brent is about $107.9 on 19 Oct (Trading Economics), roughly 3.7% above the threshold with 8.5 trading days left. A driftless lognormal at about 50% annualised volatility gives about 65% for a close above $104. I shade that to 62% because this year's de-escalation headlines have repeatedly cut 6-8% in a day. The forecast is most sensitive to whether a US-Iran de-escalation headline lands before 29 Oct.

The W40 FDOH report (Oct 4-10) lists 8 counties, the count is cumulative, and over the past seven weeks it rose by about one county every two weeks. I expect roughly 0-1 more by the W42 report: 8 (40%) or 9 (33%) are most likely. The forecast is most sensitive to any new county announcing a first local case or positive mosquito pool before Oct 24.

As of Oct 19, history.md still lists only the three Oct 7 withdrawals, and no commit has changed a manuscript since Oct 8. OpenAI has preferred revising to withdrawing (14 to 1), so a new fatal flaw would need to be found, judged unfixable and logged within about 10 days. The forecast is most sensitive to whether an outside expert shows a specific result is false before Oct 29.

Core PCE has been 3.0% y/y for three months. Nowcasts that map the hot September CPI and PPI into PCE put September core at 0.32-0.34% m/m and 3.1% y/y (TD Securities, WSJ/Timiraos), clearly above the ~0.2% Sep-2025 m/m that drops out. The main uncertainty is the unrounded August level, which splits the risk toward 3.0 or 3.2.

Weekly counts held at 71-87 in E-weeks 35-40, but the partial E-week 41 daily counts point to about 62-70 as the May-October peak season winds down (NEA). I project a mild further decline for E-week 42's provisional first print, with wide tails. The forecast is most sensitive to the settled E-week 41 total.

The FDOH total was 368 at Week 40, after recent weekly additions of +62, +44 and +72 (mean about 59). Two more weeks at a slightly seasonally damped ~55 per week gives about 480, with a right skew in case the epidemic is still accelerating. The forecast depends most on the Week 41 increment due around Oct 22.

Direct leader contact has run about once every 1–3 weeks, which gives a base rate of about 12–15% for any given 2-day window. I shade that down because nothing is scheduled for 29–30 Oct, Trump is openly hostile after the 10 Oct 'new president' remarks and the diesel and Starlink disputes, the current channel runs through envoys, and it is the last week of the midterm campaign. The number is most sensitive to whether a US-brokered negotiation round lands on those dates.

The 16 Oct NEA snapshot shows 3 clusters with 10 or more cases. These are a new, growing Lentor Gardens cluster plus the long-running Bishan St 12 and Ho Ching Rd clusters, and both of those still add about 2 cases a week. Weekly cases are flat at about 70-90, so persistence dominates. Most mass is on 2-3, with the forecast most sensitive to whether Ho Ching or Bishan stops producing cases before 29 Oct.

The post has been vacant since 16 October (Wikipedia). NBC sources say Trump is unlikely to name a successor soon, and the last search took six weeks. Only about 11 days remain, and an acting deputy does not count. The main risk is a fast internal promotion of Anna Kelly, the Kalshi favourite.

The last close was 648 bp (Rava, 16 Oct), after four days of increases to near the 2026 high of about 655. Historical volatility of about ±50 bp over 9 trading days sets the width. I center slightly below the last close because the index has fallen back from this level before. The Brazilian runoff on 25 October is the main event risk, so both tails are wide.

The last three FDOH weekly reports showed 62, 44 and 72 new local cases, so the outbreak is still at its peak. Intensive spraying and the end of the mosquito season argue for a plateau or slow decline rather than further growth. The forecast is most sensitive to the Week 41 report (due ~Oct 22) and to batching of lab results.

AWS growth has accelerated from 20% to 24%, 28% and then 36.7% over four quarters, and it beat AWS consensus by roughly 2-5 pp in each of the last three. With consensus near 37-38% ($45.1B per HSBC), I expect about 40%, with wide tails. The result depends most on how much new AI capacity came online in Q3.

Recent weekly U.S. wheat net sales for 2026/27 have ranged from about 255,000 to 450,000 MT (319,900 MT in the week to Oct 8, a four-week average near 270,000 MT). Lagging HRW sales and a lower USDA export forecast offset Black Sea disruption that favours U.S. origin. The result is most sensitive to whether a large tender or flash sale lands in the week ending Oct 22, so the right tail is wide.

Day 4 of the 2023 timeline, which matches 2026's, had 103,617 votes in the final table (~90k as reported live, ordinary votes only); 2017 had 73k and COVID-era 2020 had 110k. Closing enrolment before voting opens and a larger pre-voting roll roughly offset each other, so the forecast is anchored near 90-95k. It is most sensitive to whether the 2026 live table shows ordinary votes only or combined votes, and to campaign enthusiasm.

AMZN sits at about $253 (Oct 16 close $250.00, Oct 19 pre-market $255) with 9 sessions plus an earnings print priced at ±7.6% by options. That is roughly ±11% of combined 1σ uncertainty, so mass spreads across all five buckets, peaking slightly in the bucket containing spot. The forecast is most sensitive to the direction of the AWS/capex surprise on Oct 29.

Amazon usually reports net sales at or slightly above the top of its guidance (about +0.4% on average over the last 9 quarters), and Q3 guidance is $197-202B. That guide is held down by Prime Day moving into Q2, while AWS is growing 37% and FX stayed close to the guide's assumption, so I centre just above the $202B consensus. The number is most sensitive to how much Prime Day timing actually removed from Q3.

Brent settled at $109.86 on 16 October and was around $108 on 19 October, with the Iran war and Hormuz disruption ongoing. I model a random walk with fat tails at about 55% annualised volatility over 8 trading days. I add a 12% chance of a US–Iran Hormuz deal, which would send the price back toward the low $90s, as after the April ceasefire. The forecast is most sensitive to whether that deal happens before 29 October.

Most crew missing after open-sea sinkings are never recovered within two weeks; HS Dignity sank and Bulgaria abandoned the search on 14 Oct, so ~52% on 0. The upside is Wine Trader, still afloat with crew likely trapped in its burned accommodation, so a batch recovery once it can be boarded is plausible; the forecast is most sensitive to whether that boarding happens before 29 Oct.

Normal October 2026 nights ran at 128-149 drones (question background), and the night of 18-19 Oct had 243 shot down (Ukrinform), so the median sits slightly above the normal cluster because the winter energy campaign is under way. The forecast is most sensitive to whether 29-30 Oct is a massive-strike night; I put about 12% on 400 or more drones, which gives a long right tail.

The Supreme Court has refused every request to stay the SIR since 2025 and upheld it in May 2026. On 15 October it only issued notice on the INDIA bloc's plea for suspension. The one hearing inside the window, on 28 October, concerns a Delhi plea for disclosure and re-inclusion, and an order there is procedural, which resolves NO. The main risk is a broad 28 October order that bars finalisation or deletions of the Delhi roll.

The repository has had one content update since launch (the 10-07 batch, merged 10-08: 6 new formalizations, bringing it to 300/719) and nothing for 11 days, so the status quo of 300 is the base case. YES needs a new batch with at least one new top-line formalization recorded in history.md by 10-29. OpenAI's public pledge to keep adding formalizations, and a possible ~3-week cadence, keep that chance material.

The count is 22 on Wikipedia today. The NHC gives disturbance EP94 a 90% chance of forming within 7 days, so Vance (the 23rd storm) is likely by Oct 29, at about 82%. Since 2014, 1-2 storms have been named in Oct 17-29 in 11 of 12 seasons, but no second area is flagged yet, so a 24th storm sits at about 26%. The forecast depends most on whether EP94 actually reaches tropical-storm strength.

Russia has rejected every limited Black Sea truce since August 2026, most recently on 2 and 9 October, and on 12 October rejected the 60-day ceasefire, insisting on a comprehensive settlement only; Kyiv will accept a maritime truce only bundled with an energy truce, and that truce collapsed within a day on 11-12 October. The one Black Sea deal that ever took effect needed about 3 months of Turkey/UN mediation, and the March 2025 US-announced deal never took effect, so a deal confirmed by both governments and in effect within 11 days is very unlikely; the main risk is a sudden US-brokered package with sanctions relief.

The official cumulative count was already 4,793 after week 41. The 1,703 the question calls cumulative is that week's figure. Three more weeks of about 1,500-2,500 closures (growth slowing, sentinel 12.81, +13%) put the cumulative total near 10,000. I keep 35% on a weekly-figure resolution near 1,900. The forecast is most sensitive to which figure the resolver uses.

In week 41 only Okinawa (31.34, falling) was at or above 30, and the next prefectures were at 20-22 (Kanagawa, Saitama, Chiba). National growth is slow (11.35 to 12.81, +13% a week), and week 42 contains a holiday. In past seasons a national average of about 15-17 has meant 0-1 prefectures at warning level. The forecast is most sensitive to whether Hokkaido (x1.76 in week 41) and Kanagawa keep accelerating.

The mayorista has stayed within 1,506-1,525 since September while the BCRA keeps buying, and it closed at 1,518 on 16 Oct (Rava, press). The forecast assumes a small upward drift (REM and year-end consensus near 1,600) and wider tails to the upside. It is most sensitive to whether the 1,505-1,530 corridor holds through 29 Oct.

No US land strike on Iran has been confirmed since about 1 September, and Israel and Iran have not exchanged fire since June. Trump has publicly pledged no attack before the 3 November midterms, and Israel says it will not act without US approval, so a deliberate campaign on 29-30 October is unlikely. The residual risk is a limited US self-defense strike after an IRGC attack on US forces, or Israeli retaliation if Iran strikes around Israel's 27 October election.

USD/KRW is at 1,331.24 on Trading Economics for Oct 19, 0.66% below the threshold. With 8 trading days of about 0.3-0.5% daily volatility, a random walk gives roughly 26-34%. The won's three-month strengthening trend pulls the number down. Policy support near 1,330 (NPS dollar buying) and a 25-33% chance of a Fed hike on Oct 28 keep upside risk alive, and that hike is the factor the forecast is most sensitive to.

The US has refused Tomahawks for Ukraine for 13 months, including when the Pentagon cleared a transfer, so the base rate for an 11-day window is about 1%. Current conditions push further toward NO: the Iran war used more than 1,000 Tomahawks and refilling the stock will take years, allied arms sales are paused, and Trump is openly hostile to Zelensky while doing deals with Putin. Only a sudden break with Moscow would change this.

ECDC's Week 42 report (data to 14 Oct) gives 19 countries, and only two more weekly reports fall before resolution. Few or no countries are usually added after mid-October, but this record 2026 season has kept adding late reporters (+3 in two weeks), so a 20th is quite possible (Türkiye, counted in 2025, is the likeliest). The forecast is most sensitive to whether any new country reports a first human case before 28 Oct.

Past US threats against Ukraine aid rarely became acknowledged pauses within 11 days, and every on-record US and NATO statement (Whitaker 13 Oct, NATO officials) calls PURL deliveries ongoing, if delayed. The risk to that view is the partial hold on PURL-funded Patriots that Hegseth has not signed (Zelensky, 18 Oct), alongside the escalating refinery-strike dispute. The forecast is most sensitive to whether a named Ukrainian official starts calling those Patriots stopped rather than not approved.

Before October, strikes off Romania ran at about one a month (about 3% a day); the October wave hit 7 ships on 5 of 16 days, but nothing has been confirmed since 15 Oct, and Romanian air defences and NATO attention are rising. The forecast is most sensitive to whether the Russian campaign against shipping anchored off Sulina resumes before 29 Oct; it rests on the blacksea.america2.news tracker and AP/Reuters-based reporting.

The question cites about 9-10 a day, but hormuz.now rebuilt its data on 19 Oct and its first full day shows 0. AIS-only series such as PortWatch (2-4 a day) and the mid-October escalation (about 20 attacks, two sinkings) support a low count. About 35% is on 0, and the forecast is most sensitive to whether the new pipeline records any crossings at all.

Formal suspension with a resumed session is rare for CBD meetings: 2 of about 17, including the most recent, COP16 in Cali. UN talks that fail usually close and defer items, which resolves NO here. A heavy finance and budget agenda and the same Friday-close calendar as Cali roughly offset the post-Cali lessons and the Rome roadmap that defers the hardest finance decisions to COP18-19. The forecast is most sensitive to whether the finance and budget texts are still bracketed going into the 30 October closing plenary.

Kaiser–CNA NorCal contracts have historically settled months after expiry, either on a strike deadline or after long drift (2015, 2018, 2022: TAs 78 or more days after expiry). As of 12 Oct 2026 the sides had held 17 sessions, wage proposals had barely been exchanged, a strike authorization vote was under way and dates were being booked through December. Only two sessions (21–22 Oct) fall before the cutoff, so a full TA by 29 Oct is very unlikely.

Anchored on the same four days in 2023: about 294k as reported live during the campaign (339k in today's table, which now includes special votes). Nudged up for the rising advance-vote share and a tight National-Labour race. The result is most sensitive to whether the 2026 daily page counts special votes and to the day-1 turnout pace.

The Ohio Supreme Court usually takes about 74 days to decide whether to hear an appeal, and the NCAA's response is not due until about early November. The court's 14 October stay is temporary, lasting only until it has considered the 19 October briefs, so its next order is most likely a ruling on the stay, which does not count. The main route to YES is a fast dismissal as moot because of DeWine's executive order, and that looks unlikely because the NCAA disputes the order in federal court.

By law (NLRA 8(g)) a strike on 29–30 October needs 10 days' notice, so a notice served by 19–20 October. On 15 October Kaiser said it had received none, and CNA's press page through 17 October shows no vote result, notice or strike date. Bargaining sessions on 21–23 October and dates booked into December point to any escalation coming in November at the earliest. The only real YES path is an unreported notice served on 19–20 October.

The Cali Fund has received three tiny deposits in about 20 months, totalling $7,085 (AFP, 20 Oct 2026), so the most likely value on 31 Oct is unchanged. The main upside is two small pledges worth $3,571 that may be paid (which would give about $10.7k), plus a thin tail for a real COP17 transfer. The forecast is most sensitive to whether any COP17 announcement turns into a deposit booked by 31 Oct.

Base rates for a BLA that has passed its late-cycle meeting and inspections point to ~60-70%. I lower that because the FDA's preliminary view is that INO-3107 is ineligible for accelerated approval now that Papzimeos (51% complete response, full approval) exists. INO-3107's year-1 complete-response rate is 28%, INOVIO is not pursuing traditional approval, and the FDA still had not addressed eligibility or the confirmatory trial as of August. The forecast hinges on that unresolved eligibility call.

Every SIR final roll whose last-set date arrived was published on that date (Bihar, Kerala, West Bengal, UP, Odisha, Punjab), so the question is whether the ECI extends Andhra Pradesh a fifth time. It has done so four times (Sep 22 → Oct 30), but hearings were 99.9% done by late September and the Supreme Court is pressing for local-body polls. Most sensitive to whether a new ECI communique appears around Oct 22–28.

BTC is at ~$81.3k (CoinGecko, Oct 20) and needs about +4.5% by the single 00:00 UTC Oct 31 snapshot. Deribit implied vol (DVOL ~38) puts $85k ~0.68 sigma away: ~25% lognormal, ~20% fat-tailed. Mild negative momentum and October ETF outflows (-$617M) shade it to ~22%; the Oct 28 FOMC, ~86% priced as a hold, is the main event risk. Most sensitive to a break out of the $79-84k range before month-end.

On 10-13 the defence team formally committed to file at the Suwon High Court within October, dropping every other option, and on 10-14 it named the week of 10-19 (YTN, Dailian, Segye). Filing is unilateral and cheap, and eleven days remain. The main risk is slippage: the petition was still undrafted on 10-14, the lawyer said the date could change, and no filing had been reported by 10-20.

New Zealand are much stronger: they lost only 22-24 to Australia, and Fiji are missing Kikau, Kamikamica and Bula, so a margin near 19 points is the central estimate. But this is likely a playoff for a semi-final spot, and both previous World Cup meetings (2017, 2022) were decided by 6 points or less. The forecast is most sensitive to the unseen bookmaker handicap.

The Brewers (MLB-best 103-59, home field) face the Rays, who won the ALCS 4-2 on Oct 19. Sportsbooks and Kalshi price Milwaukee at about 59-62% after vig (DraftKings -155/+135), which matches the ~55-60% base rate for Series favorites with home field. The forecast mainly tracks that market price; a short series between two elite pitching staffs stays close to a coin flip.

The national figure was 12.81 in week 41 (5-11 Oct), growing about 13-16% a week; past waves that crossed 10-15 (2023, 2024, 2025) all kept rising over the next two weeks, by 1.8x to 4.7x. This early, slow-moving season most resembles 2023, so I project modest compounding to about 16, with a right skew. The forecast is most sensitive to whether the week 42 print shows a plateau.

USDA reportedly said on 2026-10-19 that Columbus will reopen to Mexican cattle on October 26 (Meatingplace; Chihuahua union reports agree). The two earlier announced reopenings this year both happened on schedule despite nearby screwworm cases. The forecast is most sensitive to a pause triggered by new detections before October 26, and to whether the APHIS page reflects the reopening by October 30.

Centred on the live spot price of ~$82.8k (Yahoo and CoinGecko, Oct 20), with a fat-tailed spread sized to Deribit's 30-day implied volatility of ~37% over the 10.1 days to the 00:00 UTC Oct 31 close. The low tail is slightly heavier because of the $80k support level, negative ETF flows this month and the Oct 27-28 FOMC meeting. The forecast is most sensitive to whether $80k holds.

Since May the national active count has stayed in a mean-reverting 1,700–2,100 band, and the latest Senasica prints are 1,968–1,976 (14–17 Oct). A rain-driven northern surge (Chihuahua 85 → 176) adds mild upward pressure, while cooler weather and sterile-fly releases cap it. The forecast is most sensitive to the week-42 report around 23 October.

A random walk from December Brent at about $109-110 (settled $108.79 on 20 Oct, per Reuters), with OVX near 51 implying roughly +/-$9.5 over 8 trading days, and fat tails for US-Iran deal or escalation headlines. The median is shaded about $1 lower because the December contract expires on 30 Oct and Barchart's continuous series may already show the January contract, about $3 cheaper in backwardation.

Cerimedo is held under two independent six-month preventive-detention orders. An appeals chamber reconfirmed the femicide order on 7 Oct, and no cessation hearing or release had been reported as of 22 Oct (Infobae, La Razón, Opinión). Even his lawyer only points to November. The small residual rests on the fallout from the Attorney General's arrest, which could give the defence grounds to challenge both orders.

In an active campaign, a three-day window has a reported refinery hit about 60-75% of the time (Oct 2026: Volgograd, Omsk, Salavat, Ukhta, Ryazan). But no refinery hit has been confirmed since Ryazan on 15 Oct. US pressure peaks before the 3 Nov midterms, and Zelensky has offered a 30-day refinery pause in exchange for Patriots. The forecast turns on whether Kyiv is quietly holding back on refineries; a confirmed hit before 29 Oct would move it sharply up.

The First Committee in-favour count on the TPNW resolution has held at 118-124 since 2020 (122 in 2024, 121 in 2025; UN press, Reaching Critical Will) with frozen voting blocs; the question background's '144 in 2024' is the Japan road-map resolution, not this one. Median 122 with only ~3-4% on the question's 130+ range; most sensitive to a bloc of umbrella states or abstainers switching before the Review Conference.

The trend gives the answer here. The DRC count was about 9,850 confirmed cases on about 23 Oct (CDC 9,816; INSP-derived 9,876), and daily increments have held at 55-76 for a month (ECDC, CDC, UKHSA). Eight more days at about 63/day gives about 10,350. The result is most sensitive to whether incidence breaks out of that plateau, and to which reporting date (30 or 31 Oct) the resolver picks.

Centred on the ~$905-935M sell-side consensus, which needs September ARR of about $4.5B, up from the $3.0B June run-rate; that step-up rests on Microsoft tranches delivered in July-August and late-Q2 capacity coming online. Nudged slightly up for two straight beats, with about ±6% tails for Nebius's capacity-timing surprises; most sensitive to whether activations inside the quarter slipped.

Past Kyrgyz presidential races drew 59-83 applications with strong last-days surges (2020: 5 eleven days out became 65). But 2026 has only 3 after five weeks, under a consolidated incumbent with no serious opposition, so I expect a muted surge to the mid-teens with a wide right tail. The forecast is most sensitive to whether a language certificate now gates filing itself.

EU storage was 74.64% on 30 Oct and net withdrawals of ~0.13 pp/day were already under way (AGSI+). Past early-November drawdowns ran from 0 to -0.25 pp/day, and tight LNG supply points to the faster end, so I project ~-0.16 pp/day over 13 days. The result is most sensitive to whether a cold, windless spell arrives before 12 Nov; the forecast SSW mostly lands later.

Bookmakers price Germany at about 76% with the margin removed (FanDuel -475) to win in a Belgrade match UEFA has ordered played behind closed doors, against a Serbia side with 0 points from four games. I shade that down to 70% for Germany's poor finishing under Klopp (one win and three goals in four games) and the risk of a draw. The forecast is most sensitive to the November squad news and to whether other bookmakers confirm the ~1.21 price.

Government-party (Fine Gael) PMB that the Government did not oppose in the Seanad in 2023, with a Programme for Government spiking commitment and no Government bill: most likely the question is put and agreed without a division. The rest is a claimed and postponed division (~11%) or the debate not concluding or the item not being taken (~13%). Most sensitive to a Government timed amendment or any TD claiming a division.

Known Q3 revenue of NT$3,027bn at Hon Hai's 2.4-2.8% net margin gives 72-85bn. Subsidiary FII's record RMB 16.6bn Q3 profit (+26% QoQ) and a flat NT dollar over the quarter (so no repeat of Q2's FX loss) centre it near 80bn. The forecast is most sensitive to one-off non-operating items and the minority-interest share.

July (+0.4%) and August (+0.1%) are published, and the monthly path gives a Q3 carry-over of about 0.73% q/q if September is flat. Soft September indicators (retail -0.4%, weaker ONS real-time data) pull the centre to about 0.67%, so 0.6 and 0.7 are near coin-flips. Most sensitive to September's print and to revisions to July/August.

The base rate for League A is about 43% home / 27% draw / 30% away. The Paris-leg market (about 66% France at home) implies France are roughly 100 Elo stronger, which nearly cancels Italy's home advantage at San Siro. France's better 2026 record (World Cup semi-final, 4-1 v Belgium) tilts it slightly to France: Italy 31%, Draw 28%, France 41%. The forecast is most sensitive to November squad news (Mbappé, possible France rotation) and to the first bookmaker lines.

The status quo dominates a 10-day window, since impeachment and the Tennessee Senate-seat route cannot remove him before 12 Nov. Markets price about 24-31% for an exit announced by Dec 1-Dec 31 (Polymarket, Kalshi, GJOpen), and only part of that falls in this window with immediate effect. The forecast is most sensitive to whether Trump makes a Sessions/Esper-style immediate firing in the days after the 3 Nov midterms.

Decree-laws put to the Diputación Permanente after a dissolution are almost always convalidated, and all six groups that make up the 35-34 majority, including the pivotal PNV, already voted for this text on 2 Oct and PNV has confirmed its yes. The forecast is most sensitive to one ally defecting or abstaining, possibly over the Urda crash, and to the 12 Nov session, the only viable date, actually being held.

MinEk's monthly-indicator estimate for Q3 2026 is +0.6% y/y (29 Oct); Rosstat's preliminary print has matched MinEk within ±0.1 pp in 5 of 7 recent quarters (misses: -0.3 in Q1 2025, +0.4 in Q2 2026), so the median stays at 0.6 with a slightly heavier upper tail. Most sensitive to whether the Q2-2026-style upside gap recurs.

From 15 October to 2 November 2026, normal nights ran 88-280 drones (median about 150), with waves of 580 (14-15 Oct) and 433 (31 Oct-1 Nov). Large strikes have come every 5-17 days, so 12-13 November is a draw from a right-skewed mixture with about a 14 % chance of a wave night. The forecast is most sensitive to whether that night is one of Russia's massed strikes.

This is a one-month step from September's 4.1%. October 2025 (+0.49% m/m, including a 6.6% electricity hike) drops out of the base. With no electricity hike in October 2026 (delayed past the election) and a typical October m/m of about 0.3-0.4%, the rate edges down to about 3.9-4.0%, against upward food, core and PPI momentum. The forecast is most sensitive to October food and administered prices.

Clear-favourite MVP winners since 2014 were ~50% unanimous and none got fewer than 28; Crow-Armstrong (40-40, 45 HR, MLB-leading 10.6 fWAR) swept all 38 first-place votes in MLB.com's final poll. Most sensitive to how many writers reward Ohtani's two-way half-season (1.79 ERA, 85.2 IP).

Paraguay (ranked 33rd, ~85% win implied by Megapari's 1X2) are heavy favourites over a leaky Singapore (6-0 loss to Malaysia on 1 Oct, 7-0 to Korea in 2024), so I expect roughly 2.3 Paraguay goals plus 0.5 from Singapore. I shade that down because Alfaro's low-scoring, clean-sheet style (2026 matches averaged about 2.0 total goals) and likely rotation in a friendly four days before Japan pull the total toward 2-3. The total is most sensitive to Paraguay's November squad and the attacking intent of their starting XI.

Weekly data (Oct-to-date +1.14% by 26 Oct) imply ~1.20% m/m, i.e. ~7.09% y/y against October 2025's +0.50%; Rosstat's monthly print has tended to land below the weeklies (-0.06 to -0.36 pp, two Octobers running), so the distribution centres near 7.0% with ~0.2 pp spread. Most sensitive to the monthly-minus-weekly gap.

The October 2025 base in the new series is roughly flat on September 2025, so October 2026 is about 5.54% plus that month's m/m change. Sticky onion and food momentum and the festive season suggest about +0.45% m/m, consistent with India Ratings (~6.0%), ICRA (>6%) and RBI's Q3 6.0%. Falling silver and gold and easing tomato prices temper it. The forecast is most sensitive to late-October vegetable prices and to the exact October 2025 base index.

hormuz.now's own series is the outside view: 4-13 commercial crossings a day since 20 Oct, with a 7-day average of 9.1 on 1 Nov. The median stays near it because Iran has not accepted the Qatar seven-day plan. The tails are fat in both directions: a deal implemented in early November could, as after the June MoU, take crossings to 20-40 (about 10-14%), and renewed US strikes after the 3 Nov midterms could cut them to 2-4.

The October 2025 base month's +0.5% m/m pulls a flat October 2026 to ~6.3% y/y; the end of the larger 2026 electricity/gas subsidy and higher October crude should lift October m/m to about +0.2-0.3%, partly offset by falling rice prices. Most sensitive to how the BOJ records the subsidy end in October.

AAA regular is $4.1694 and needs another ~12 c drop in 11 days; the October trend alone is a coin flip, but wholesale gasoline fell to a 9-week low (~$2.99) on 11/2, leaving the pump price above its likely equilibrium. Most sensitive to whether the Iran-diplomacy-driven crude drop reverses after the Nov 3 midterms.

The ministry's confirmed count has been flat at 5 since Oct 27 with surgical exposure stopped and 3 patients now negative, so the status quo of 5 is the base case; a right tail to 6-9 reflects the pending suspected deaths and possible additional cases.

Oct 2025 placements (21,284) grown by the +2% y/y pace of Sept placements and Oct-1 eggs in incubators, cross-checked with the Sept-to-Oct step, gives about 21,700; HPAI losses are tiny against monthly placements; most sensitive to the noisy seasonal step and NASS estimation error.

Week 42 was 7.6% with weekly ratios of about 1.25 and broad regional growth; two more weeks at that pace, tempered by early-season noise and signs of West Coast flattening, give about 11.5%. The forecast is most sensitive to whether weekly growth stays above about 1.15x or stalls.

AMAT has met or beaten the midpoint of its guidance in each of the last 7 quarters, by +1.5-3.4% in the last three, so I start from the $10,250M midpoint and add a ~$170M typical beat, with a fat lower tail for shipment timing/China risk. The forecast is most sensitive to whether the unusually large guided step-up is shipped in full.

Early-November weeks were builds in all of 2019-2025 (median +3.9M), but 2026 has four straight draws and heavy exports, so I blend them for a median near +0.7M with wide fat tails (52-week SD about 5.6M). Most sensitive to whether the seasonal refinery-turnaround build appears despite strong exports.

Peltola leads polls by ~2-3 points and late-counted Alaska ballots have consistently tilted 1-3 points toward Democrats, offset by Alaska's history of polls understating Republicans; markets (~70-74%) are slightly higher. Most sensitive to the election-night margin.

Last print 1.9% and seven private trackers at 1.8-2.1% (mean 1.94%) outweigh the stale REM of 1.7%, with fuel and food pushing up and flat FX and falling clothing pulling down; most sensitive to whether INDEC food and regulated components follow the hot weekly trackers.

Only ~15% of AL MVPs since 2000 were unanimous (~40% for runaways); Alvarez is a near-certain winner but got only 29/38 first-place votes in the last expert poll and is a DH who cooled late; most sensitive to BBWAA voters consolidating beyond expert polls.

First-published SA total changes are small in normal years but 2026 has been volatile; two -0.5% months and a ~13% jump in October pump prices (inflating nominal fuel spending) argue for a modest rebound, tempered by falling consumer confidence. Most sensitive to whether October seasonal adjustment and fuel-volume weakness offset the price effect.

NHL home teams win ~54%; Florida and Detroit are close in quality (Florida's 2025-26 record was worse, early 2026-27 slightly better) and Florida's Barkov/Marchand absences offset home ice and Detroit's Larkin turmoil. Most sensitive to goalie health on both sides and the Florida returns.

Weekly counts have swung between 0 and 5 (SE 38-42: 3, 5, 0, 5, 5) and the same weeks in 2025 gave 2-6, so I centre on 4 with a right tail; the target is two editions beyond the latest known (SE 42 = 5), and the count is most sensitive to whether covid or metapneumovirus growth in the Southeast capitals continues.

AST must finish an art. 8 requirements check and organise commissions in six cities before posting dates, and typical practice and a 15-day notice norm make a calendar by 12 Nov less likely than not; speed on scores and service pressure keep it plausible.

The authors' own README says they will not rush the unreadable 4D draft and will proceed at a human pace, with no stated arXiv plan; recent work is on 3D, and repo files do not count. The main YES path is a hurried personal-site or arXiv posting under priority pressure.

The revised Q2 level (4.1% y/y) and an extra working day carry over to about 4.0%, but weak September construction and retail data and bank nowcasts of 3-3.5% pull the centre to 3.8%. Most sensitive to the actual Q3 q/q, which the banks disagree on.

The series averaged ~0.4% per month over the last 13 months (0.47% over the last six) with a 5.0% annual rate, and inflationary pipeline indicators (ISM prices 77.9, record selling-price PMI) support persistence; a partial payback of September's +3.4% transport and warehousing jump is the main downside risk, and the forecast is most sensitive to that component.

The October OMR figure (-2.6) is the anchor because the last revision shrank to -0.1 mb/d, with a slight lean to a further cut since Hormuz re-escalated and Brent ran $109-117 in late October. The forecast is most sensitive to whether a US-Iran deal or new strikes land before the IEA's cut-off.

The court's Brown postings are bursty (0 in Sept, 3 in Oct 19-30) and the Nov listing is empty on Nov 3; a committee report or scope-expansion order after Brown's Oct 30 no-show could add posts, but s.360 confidentiality and slow Council timing (Newman: 32-51 days report-to-order) favour 0-2. Most sensitive to whether the court posts the committee's next order.

DOJ says it is actively presenting to a D.C. grand jury with a Nov 5 Speedy Trial deadline, which would normally mean about a 60 % chance, but D.C. grand juries have repeatedly refused politically charged indictments (Hutchinson on Oct 27), the evidence is old and thin, and timing and scope risks remain. The forecast is most sensitive to whether the Nov 5 deadline is binding.

DOE nuclear sites rarely state a fire's cause publicly within about two weeks; LANL's June 2026 glovebox fire had none after 24 days. Six days after this fire, SRS and DOE have said only that an investigation is underway, and the site's releases since then are unrelated. The main upside risk is a preliminary cause released under pressure from the press and over the retracted radiological-release notice.

The value is the total number of unique forecasters after 730 days, divided by 730. The bot ecosystem has about 130-175 bots per season, and the testing area is the recommended practice space, so about 240 unique accounts over two years is the central case. The forecast is most sensitive to how many new bots actually test on this question, which I could not observe directly.

After eight years the party out of the White House usually wins it back (since 1948 the in-party has won a third straight term only once). On top of that, Democrats swept the 2026-11-03 midterms, and Kalshi and Polymarket price them at 66.5-67.5% (2026-11-08). I shade slightly toward 50/50 because the race is two years out and the nominees are unknown, which gives Democratic 65%, Republican 33%, Other 2%.

FY2026 outlays were $7.396T (Treasury MTS). CBO's February 2026 baseline implies about $8.15-8.2T for FY2028, which includes about $118B of payments pulled into FY2028 because 1 Oct 2028 is a Sunday. I trim slightly for FY2026's undershoot of CBO and skew the tails upward for a possible 2027-28 recession and the pending defense buildup.

outcome: Second Stage granted — the Dáil gives the Bill a Second Reading on 12 November 2026

thesis: He attended about 5 of 8 recent Ukraine-related EU summits in person, and Ukraine's 2027 financing is the central item here. Against that, a special summit dominated by the MFF budget, the Feb 2024 video precedent, intense peace diplomacy and a cancelled late-October Brussels trip pull it to a coin flip. The most sensitive fact is whether Costa's invitation specifies in-person participation.

The forecast is a 9-session random walk from the 13 Nov close of R$7.81 (Yahoo), with about 6% daily volatility and fat tails. The median is shaded slightly down for the 2 Dec dilution vote and give-back after a +39% week. It is most sensitive to whether the extreme post-election volatility persists.

Typical post-midterm days on the resolution archive run 4-17 posts (Nov 8-14, 2026), and Thanksgiving 2025 had only 5; the 40-a-day headline is a mean driven by rare sprees. The forecast is most sensitive to whether a news trigger sets off a holiday spree like Christmas 2025 (126 posts), which the right tail covers.

Fat-tailed 9-session random walk from the R$0.68 Yahoo close of 13 Nov, blending calm November trading with October's crash regime and a slight downward drift for an equity in judicial recovery; no catalyst scheduled before 27 Nov and no reverse split pending. Most sensitive to an unscheduled court or creditor shock.

An 8-session random walk from the 13 Nov close of 172,458 (Yahoo), widened for post-runoff volatility (sigma ~4.3%, fat tails). The fiscal-package votes in the Senate (17 Nov) and Chamber (~18 Nov) are the main event risk, with a mild left skew. The forecast is most sensitive to how the Chamber treats PLP 299.

Every Spanish general election since 2015 has had a multi-candidate debate with at least three leaders. PSOE and PP negotiators fixed the Academia's four-way for Thursday 26 November (EFE, 14 Nov; Vozpópuli, 15 Nov), and the three-of-four threshold covers one leader dropping out. The main risk is that the date, not yet officially confirmed, slips or the format collapses late.

Both Model Studio pricing pages already list a non-preview qwen4-max with pay-as-you-go prices as of 16 Nov 2026: $1.5/$4.5 per 1M tokens internationally, CNY 10/30 on the China page. That already meets the resolution criteria. The residual risk is Alibaba pulling the row before 27 Nov or the resolver misreading it.

Detroit is a 2.5-point home favourite, which sportsbooks price at about 57-60% before the 15 Nov games. Since then the Lions won 35-10 in Munich to reach 7-2, but lost edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson to a reported season-ending knee injury, which takes about 1-2 pp off. The forecast is most sensitive to quarterback health after the 22 Nov games and to how far the line moves on the Hutchinson news.

The SE 43 and SE 44 InfoGripe bulletins both report national COVID-19 SRAG growth, and the wave is still spreading across Centro-Sul states, with the Covid share of positives up from 8.5% to 11.5%. Growth signals tend to persist, and either the 6-week or the 3-week horizon is enough for YES. Against that, Mato Grosso is already decelerating, counts are small, and past waves (2023) turned to desaceleração about two editions later. The forecast is most sensitive to whether the wave peaks before 21 November.

The question's Dallas -1.5 is the stale May opener, set before Hurts was lost. Dallas was -4.5 at Philadelphia in Week 7 and won 38-21, so the home rematch implies about -7 against a 2-7 Eagles side on a seven-game skid with a backup-of-a-backup quarterback. Applying the NFL margin distribution at -7 gives 47/24/29, shaded for not having seen the current line, which is the number this forecast is most sensitive to.

Two-week relative returns among four highly correlated chip stocks are close to a coin toss, so the probabilities follow volatility. AMD and Micron are the most volatile, and Nvidia's Nov 17 earnings (about ±10% implied) lift it to about 26%. The forecast is most sensitive to the Nvidia print.

The forecast starts from October's 2.6% and a flat November 2025 base. The 2026 summer electricity/gas subsidy was larger than 2025's (3.5 vs 2.0 yen/kWh) and drops out in the November index, adding about +0.15 pp; rice deflation and slowing processed food roughly offset the heavier November price-hike calendar. The forecast is most sensitive to the size of that energy base effect.

The cabinet has deferred this referral for over three weeks under pressure from Hezbollah, Amal and Berri, so the base rate for a decision in the two remaining sessions is low (~15-20%). The 13 November Aoun-Salam commitment to put it on the agenda soon raises the odds, but being on the agenda is not approval. Most sensitive to whether it appears on the ~19-20 November agenda.

Single stolen sources in Mexico are usually recovered within about a week, but here nine boxes were looted by several people and none had been found nine days later. The FGR has since reclassified the cargo as medical material, and the alert is heading for a wind-down, not a formal 'all nine secured' statement. The main path to YES is the FGR's identified suspect leading to a bulk recovery announced federally.

The bill has been stalled since May. The government is still 5-6 votes short of the 37 it needs (31-32 counted by La Nacion and Infobae on 15 Nov), the dictamen on 17 Nov is uncertain, and December extraordinary sessions are an openly named fallback. A text that suspends the PASO only for the presidential race would resolve NO even if it passes. The forecast is most sensitive to whether a dictamen covering all categories is signed on 17 Nov.

The forecast is a random walk from the Nov 13 close of 24,922, nine sessions out, with a standard deviation of about 5% and fat tails. Volatility is high after the 5.5% drop on Nov 5, and Nvidia's earnings, Anthropic's IPO and the PCE release all fall inside the window. The width of the distribution matters more than its centre.

The 12 Nov bulletin stands at 20,701 with 9 editions left before 26 Nov. The October run-rate (~8-12 per edition) gives ~20,800, and the backlog push (147 cases classified on 12 Nov, 695 still under study) adds a right-skewed batch allowance. The forecast is most sensitive to whether Jalisco-style batch confirmations continue after the PAHO meeting.

The BCP's own timeline (exclusion balance ~22 Nov, tender/transfer ~27 Nov) lands right on the 27 Nov cutoff, and the Cefisa precedent took 31 days to name recipients (~2 Dec here); so 'nothing public yet' narrowly leads (42%) over tender-only (30%) and named (28%), most sensitive to whether the exclusion balance closes on time.

hormuz.now's own daily series has held at 4-13 crossings a day (median 6) for four weeks, with the 7-day average drifting down to ~6.5 under continuing attacks and the US blockade. A Qatari interim deal is pending but unimplemented, so it widens only the upper tail. The forecast is most sensitive to whether a reopening is implemented before 26 Nov.

Anchored on the October IPCA-15 (+0.32%). Food is accelerating and airfares are turning up (IPC-S +0.38%, IPC-Fipe +0.48% in early November), offset by the soft full October IPCA (0.14%) and a continuing electricity drag under the green flag. The forecast is most sensitive to food and airfares in late October and early November.

CDC's NCHS-verified count (6 as of 12 Nov) lags the states' 10 and rose +1 and +2 in its last two weekly updates. With one or two refreshes left before 26 Nov (Thanksgiving may cost one), it most likely reaches 7-8. The outcome is most sensitive to how fast NCHS verifies the two deaths announced on 13 Nov.

The status quo (8 teams, no Russia, as of 13 Nov) usually holds over a 10-day window. The IIHF has inserted Russia for Norway at the World Juniors despite Canada's visa refusal, but only in a schedule sent to federations; the public WJC page still shows Norway. Nothing indicates a decision yet for Ostrava, where the Czech government refuses visas. The forecast is most sensitive to whether the IIHF publishes a Germany-to-Russia swap on the public Ostrava pages before 26 Nov.

The 2023 debates (5.9M cara a cara, 4.16M three-way) are the anchor: linear TV is now flat and November viewing is higher, but a third leaders' event in a week dilutes interest. The figure depends most on whether the 26 Nov debate is a multi-channel Academia signal with all four leaders (about 6M+) or a single-network or empty-chair event (about 3.5M).

Contested EU Ukraine-financing items were agreed at the first summit where they were tabled 0 of 3 times; this special summit, which Costa expects to decide, lifts that. No tabled top-up proposal, four refusing states and Merz's push for an all-27 deal tied to the MFF point to 'address/revert' wording and a December deal; the forecast is most sensitive to whether the draft conclusions carry 'agrees to provide' language with opt-outs.

All four Anwar-era budget third readings (2023–2026) and, as far as found, all committee-stage allocations passed by voice vote. This year the opposition did not even force a division at the policy stage after the CSA gave the government 147 of 222 MPs. The main upside is a PN decision to put the CSA signatories on the record on the final day. A third reading slipping past 26 Nov caps it further.

Companies that first say 'no sensitive data' usually admit personal-data exposure only 1-4 months later, after forensics or a leak forces it; Maersk has been silent since 11 Nov and Whitearmor's leak deadline (~7 Dec) falls after the 27 Nov cutoff. Main upside risk: an early sample leak, or Maersk describing the data as 'non-sensitive personal data'.

Climatology gives ~23% chance of measurable rain at SFO on a late-November day, but CPC (Nov 15) flags heavy-precipitation risk for northern California Nov 24-25 and NWS an increased risk Nov 25-27 in a strong-El Nino, AR-active pattern; I lift measurable rain to ~52%. The forecast is most sensitive to whether the storm's timing lands on Nov 26 or a day earlier.

As of 12-16 Nov no DRC approval, shipment or start date had been reported for either candidate (ebolaintel, Gavi, MSF), and WHO's 4 Nov guidance of a start within 3-4 weeks of DRC approval mostly falls after 27 Nov; ChAdOx1 BDBV, with stockpiled doses, is the plausible single entry. P(0)=78%, P(1)=17%, P(2)=5%; most sensitive to a DRC approval or dose-arrival announcement in the coming days.

Gallup has had Lee flat at 39-41% for five weeks (last reading 39%, 13 Nov), so a two-week-ahead reading centres near 39 with an SD of about 2 pts. Han Duck-soo's likely release and the fight with the Chief Justice add a little downside tail. The forecast is most sensitive to whether a new shock breaks the flat regime before fieldwork on 24-26 Nov.

A committee is very likely appointed by day 17 (about 85%; large retail cases usually get one 11-16 days after filing). Whether it reaches 7 members is roughly a coin flip: large retail committees are typically 7-10, but this is a liquidation dominated by foreign vendors, and the major landlords have a conflict through bidder Catalyst. The forecast is most sensitive to the size the U.S. Trustee chooses.

In non-summer general elections, Correos has admitted 0.92M (Nov 2019) to 1.36M (2016) postal ballots, and July 2023's 2.47M was a summer effect that did not carry over to Andalucía 2026. This high-salience snap election pushes the number up from 2019, while the Vox/Ayuso calls against postal voting and CCOO's expectation of about 1M applications pull it down. The forecast is most sensitive to Correos' applications total after 19 Nov, which is not yet published.

MSTR traded at $102.93 intraday on Nov 16, only ~3% above the $100 strike with ~8.5 sessions left and ~5% daily volatility, so a driftless model gives ~42%. Bitcoin below Strategy's cost basis, no mNAV premium and MSCI deletion selling concentrated before the Nov 30 effective date tilt it up to ~47%. The forecast is most sensitive to bitcoin's path and to today's close.

On television.com.ar's program-average basis the show has run flat at 11.4-13.4 since mid-October, with the last three Thursdays at 12.5, 13.1 and 12.6. I shade the median slightly below that for late-November softening. The forecast is most sensitive to whether the Nov 19 numbers show a real downward drift.

CDEC already shows 3.44 in as of 11/16, after two storms. NWS expects 2-3.5 in liquid over the mountains Tuesday-Friday, and CPC favours a wet Thanksgiving week, so the index should gain about 5 in by Nov 26. The outcome depends most on whether Nov 20-26 stays active.

Random walk from the Nov 16 intraday $138.3 (Yahoo) over 8 sessions at ~4% daily vol (realized and ~55-60% implied); median shaded ~1% for the Dec 8 lock-up overhang, fat tails because 6-10% single-day moves recur.

Priority-review orphan NDAs are approved first-cycle ~80-85% of the time; BBP-418's significant functional Phase 3 interim results, FDA's push toward traditional approval and no AdCom lift it, while 2026's surrogate-endpoint CRLs and frequent late 3-month extensions (any slip past Nov 27 resolves NO) hold it below the ~90% Kalshi/Jefferies view. Most sensitive to whether the FDA acts exactly on time.

At a 10-day lead this is climatology: a late-November daily maximum WVHT at 46026 is typically 2 to 3.5 m. I nudged it up and fattened the right tail for the very active November swell regime (7.0 m on 14 Nov and 6.6 m on 16 Nov in the buoy's own file), an El Nino winter, and more NWS-forecast swell through 22 Nov. The biggest swing factor is whether a North Pacific storm lines up a west-northwest groundswell for Thanksgiving Day.

From October's 3.4%, the y/y rate should ease to about 3.1-3.2%: November 2025's base month had petroleum products +2.7% m/m, while November 2026 pump prices are down about 5-6% (diesel strategic-stock release, Brent ~$92), only partly offset by the +6.6% gas reference price. Most sensitive to late-November pump prices and the effective weight of petroleum products.

Display fell to 6.6M on 11 Nov after two 10K notches in nine days around the 5 Nov verdict and 9 Nov sentencing (vidIQ), against a ~-10K/month baseline; over the 16 days to 27 Nov it stays 6.60M if losses settle below ~600/day and drops to 6.59M otherwise, so ~50% 6.60M, ~40% 6.59M.

Plus Ultra stopped selling Lima on 13 Nov and intends to exit the route amid preconcurso, but had set no last-flight date and must still carry booked passengers; whether the wind-down reaches past Thursday 26 Nov is close to a coin flip, tilted to NO by acute liquidity stress and likely frequency consolidation.

Brent January has slid to ~$92 (17 Nov, Trading Economics), so $100 needs a +8.7% move in 9 sessions. War-regime volatility gives that about a 20% chance; de-escalation momentum and an IEA-projected surplus shade it lower. The forecast is most sensitive to an escalation shock in the Gulf, which has pushed Brent back over $100 four times this year.

Random walk from the 16 Nov close of $156.14 over 7 sessions that include the 17 Nov earnings reaction (options imply about ±10.6%) during a CEO-succession crisis: log-sd about 14%, fat tails, slight oversold-rebound lean. The earnings guide is the single biggest swing factor.

Regular European Councils name the pending sanctions package by number. Special summits on the MFF and Ukraine financing (Feb 2024, Mar 2025) did not. The Commission says it will table the 22nd package by 26 Nov, which keeps YES live. The forecast is most sensitive to whether the Ukraine text includes a sanctions paragraph at all, or leaves sanctions to December.

November 2026 Ukrainian Air Force overnight totals (n=12, median ~163, range 96–317) set the base. Routine nights run 90–220 and mass energy strikes every 5–7 days reach 280–600, so the upper tail is long (p90 310). The biggest unknown is whether 26–27 Nov falls on a mass-strike night.

Starting from the Nov 16 Dabom value of 7,243 won, I shade the median down slightly: farm-gate prices are falling (~5,000) on a record layer flock, the retail margin is under political pressure, and last November's analogue fell despite AI. The upper tail stays fat because a further large layer-farm HPAI outbreak before Nov 27 could add a 300-500 won step.

Alternative.me's index reads 12 today (10-13 for four days) after bitcoin's slide to about $70k, and deep-fear stretches historically last weeks. So the base case is a modest drift up into the mid-teens, with fat tails: single digits if bitcoin breaks $65k, 25-35 if it rallies back above $76k.

Stolen radiography sources are usually recovered within days or not for weeks or months. About a week after the NNRA's 11 Nov disclosure, its news page and Nigerian media show no recovery; the pit theft of six projectors looks organised, and a recovery must still be publicised by an authority before 28 Nov. The forecast is most sensitive to whether the unverified OtownGist 'recovered intact' claim reflects a real official statement.

Large, oversubscribed tech IPOs typically close day 1 at +20-30% and then fade in week one (SpaceX, Arm). Applied to a ~$78-82 offer, that matches the pre-IPO perp at ~$96 (biased high by ~7% for SpaceX) and Polymarket's modal $1.25-1.5T IPO-day cap. The forecast is most sensitive to the 18 Nov offer price and the AI-stock reaction to Nvidia's 17 Nov earnings.

Recent weekly CDC increments have been 230 to 330, adding to the 5,412 reported on 13 Nov. Pennsylvania is slowing, but Wisconsin, Indiana and Kentucky are rising, so two increments (one of them in Thanksgiving week) give about 5,900. The forecast is most sensitive to whether a 27 Nov update exists: if CDC skips or publishes early, the 4 Dec update (about 6,150) governs.

Ituri out-reported Nord-Kivu by 10 or more on 6 of the last 11 daily INSP SitReps (gap mean about +9, SD about 14), so the threshold sits near the middle. WHO reports Bunia's new cases have halved and Africa CDC reports resurgence in Beni, Butembo and Oicha, which narrows the expected gap by 26 Nov. The forecast is most sensitive to whether Nord-Kivu keeps pace with Ituri, as it did on 11 and 14 Nov.

A fund box in FSR 2026-II is likely (~80%), given the September SPK liquidation of 131 funds. But CBRT box titles are thematic: the 12 Nov Inflation Report covered the same episode as 'Recent Developments in Investment Funds', which would resolve NO here. The forecast turns on whether the FSR box title names the liquidation, as the CBRT's 4 Nov blog title did.

Peltola leads 49.98% to 45.93% and is all but certain to win the 18 Nov ranked-choice tabulation, and Senate incumbents who clearly lose almost always concede within about three weeks. But Sullivan's campaign says it will not concede before certification (target 25 Nov, two days before the deadline), and Trump/DOJ pressure gives him reasons to wait. The forecast turns mainly on whether certification happens on time and on what Sullivan says after the tabulation.

The homepage's maximum is 60 today (30-60% everything, all clearance 60% off) and it is already labelled Black Friday. A going-out-of-business sale deepens over its term, but Black Friday falls in week 3 of 16, so the mode is 60, with about 45% chance of 65 or more (mainly 'up to 70%'). Most sensitive to whether the liquidators step up the markdown for Black Friday.

Every Delhi SIR deadline has been extended, typically 1-4 days before expiry, and the ECI's fresh Annexure-A enumeration of ~47.5 lakh excluded voters only began the week of Nov 16, so a further extension of the Nov 25 claims date is likely (~82%). Reports of a ~two-week extension point to Dec 5-15, but past one-month extensions keep Dec 16+ heavily weighted.

PDP and SUPP are close to a coin flip, with PDP slightly ahead. PDP holds the seat through Wong Soon Koh, and its likely successor Joshua Ting is the Premier's political secretary; SUPP's five-term legacy claim and Kevin Lau's candidacy keep it close. GPS plans to announce all 82 candidates on 25 Nov, before the cutoff, so 'none named' is unlikely.

DHS shows 651 cases as of Nov 13, and the daily increase rose from ~15 to ~33 over Nov 3-13. Extrapolating 18-25/day for 11-14 days to the Nov 24 or Nov 27 update gives ~870-960. The result depends most on whether reactive vaccination and Thanksgiving slow ascertainment, and on whether the Nov 27 update is posted before resolution.

The EW44 bulletin already reports 102,164 cases (+4,270 in one issue), and two more issues at roughly 3,000-4,500 each point to about 109-111k in the EW46 issue. The lower tail allows for a seasonal slowdown like November 2025's (~1,600 per issue) or for the EW45 issue resolving if EW46 is posted late. The forecast is most sensitive to the EW45 increment.

In about 30% of seasons since 2015 the west group named a storm between 18 and 28 Nov. This year the 17 Nov low went unnamed and the rest of this week settles, which leaves about 22-28 Nov, a period the Met Office expects to be unsettled. The count stays at 2 unless a deep Atlantic low turns up in the last week of November.

The Nov 26 09:15 PST predicted high is 6.84 ft MLLW. Since early October the gauge has run +1.0-1.6 ft above prediction at the high tides (about +1.25 ft on Nov 15-18) because of the El Nino Kelvin wave, and nobody reports it fading. A persistence forecast therefore gives ~8.1 ft. The main sensitivity is whether the residual holds near +1.2 ft or eases or swells over the next 8 days.

On 13 Nov 2026 the BCP announced CDA fund releases 'from this Friday' (La Nación), and the FGD reported 5,800 CDA cases unblocked by 16 Nov (ABC Color). The criteria accept a past start day, so this likely already qualifies, and the 75-wage complement (legal deadline 17 Nov, extendable to 2 Dec) gives a second path. The main risk is that the resolver, anchored on the question's own background, does not count the 13 Nov statement.
